chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: Henderson's band, Hawkins and meeting Kaiser Marshall
summary: Crawford recalls King Porter Stomp and Hawkins's featured playing, and going up to meet drummer Kaiser Marshall.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: But now like -- now, so the band at that time had played in a lot of unusual keys.
Fletcher Henderson?
Yeah, that's what that was -- right, that was what you liked about the band.
Well, I guess just like King Porter Stomp came to a stop, just took me apart. Coleman Hawkins featured -- he was a real feature.
So they weren't using microphones then, were they?
I can't remember offhand, but I'm sure they had -- no, I don't know. I can't remember. But that was --
But Coleman Hawkins was featured.
Oh, that --
Now, was there anything about the drummer in the band that --
Yeah, who was playing drums? Kaiser Marshall, I think. Tall high-hot cymbals, cymbal up here and other similar gear. Kaiser was a good drummer.
And so now like did you talk -- did you talk to him after the performance?
Oh, yeah, I had to go up and meet him, yeah. I was a forward little rascal, young as I was.
What did you talk with him about. Do you remember?

Just glad to meet you, glad to meet you, Kaiser. I was sure looking forward to this. I was standing there on the dance floor (crowded), so I was happy to meet him, anybody, you know, man like him, Kaiser Marshall.
Was he playing brushes too?
Yeah, swingy brushes and things.
Did you play brushes at that time?
Yes, sir, sweeping. Oh, yes.
Now, you taught yourself how to play brushes too.
Oh, yeah, everything, brushes just looping around, that's all.
So now, when you all -- did you talk to Coleman Hawkins or any of the people in the band, other people in the band at that time?
No, I was afraid. He was too big.
(Laughter)
He was down to earth. Had I known it, I would have tried to get to him.
Uh-huh.
Yeah, but he was a big man, Coleman Hawkins. I didn't talk with him.
